name: Abilene Bombers

info: The Abilene Bombers were a professional indoor football team based in Abilene, Texas, that played from 2007 to 2013. The franchise began as the Katy Ruff Riders in the Intense Football League before relocating to Abilene following the 2008 season and becoming the Abilene Ruff Riders. Over the next several years, the team competed in the Indoor Football League, Southern Indoor Football League, and Lone Star Football League. In 2012, the franchise adopted the Abilene Bombers name and a new logo. The Bombers reached the LSFL playoffs in their final season in 2013, finishing 6–6 before falling to the Amarillo Venom in the semifinals. The franchise folded with the LSFL in 2013.

name: Alabama Empire
info: The Alabame Empire are part of the GIFL, a small soccer-plex league based in Atlanta, Georgia. The Empire started as part of the EIF, but joined the GIFL in 2025. In their 2 years as part of the GIFL, the Empire have only won 2 games, and haven't made playoffs.

name: Alabama Hammers
info: The Alabama Hammers were a professional indoor football team based in Huntsville, Alabama, that played from 2011 through 2015. The franchise began as an expansion team in the Southern Indoor Football League in 2011 before joining the Professional Indoor Football League in 2012 following the SIFL's dissolution. After struggling in their first two seasons, the Hammers hired Dean Cokinos as head coach in 2013 and enjoyed their most successful season, finishing 9–2 and winning the PIFL championship with a 70–44 victory over the Richmond Raiders. The team missed the playoffs in 2014 and finished 5–7 in 2015 before folding when the PIFL ceased operations.

name: Alabama Silverbacks
info: The Alabama Silverbacks started as the State Side Silverbacks in 2024. Despite being the home of the GIFL, the Silverbacks have only won 1 game in 3 seasons. In 2026, they rebranded as the Alabama Silverbacks.

name: Alabama Steeldogs
info: The Alabama Steeldogs, originally known as the Birmingham Steeldogs, were a professional indoor football team based in Birmingham, Alabama, that played from 2000 to 2007. The team was one of the charter franchises of AF2, the developmental league of the Arena Football League, and played its home games at the Birmingham-Jefferson Convention Complex. The Steeldogs reached the playoffs four times, with their most successful run coming in 2002 when they advanced to the National Conference Championship. After struggling in 2005, the team rebounded to make the playoffs in both 2006 and 2007. The franchise changed its name to the Alabama Steeldogs for its final season in an effort to broaden its regional appeal. Following the 2007 season, the team was deactivated after ownership was unable to secure the financing needed to continue operations.

name: Alabama Vipers
nameHistory: Tennessee Valley Vipers (2000–2004), Tennessee Valley Raptors (2005), Tennessee Valley Vipers (2006–2009), Alabama Vipers (2010)
info: The Alabama Vipers were a professional indoor football franchise based in Huntsville, Alabama, that operated from 2000 to 2010. The franchise began as the Tennessee Valley Vipers in AF2 and quickly became one of the league's strongest teams, winning five division championships and reaching the ArenaCup in 2000. After briefly competing as the Tennessee Valley Raptors in the United Indoor Football league in 2005, the Vipers returned to AF2 in 2006. Their greatest achievement came in 2008, when they went 10–6 and defeated the Spokane Shock 56–55 in overtime to win ArenaCup IX. The team joined the Arena Football League as the Alabama Vipers for the 2010 season, finishing 7–9. Following the season, the franchise relocated to Duluth, Georgia, and became the Georgia Force.

name: Albany Firebirds
info: The Albany Firebirds are a professional arena football team based in Albany, New York, playing home games at the MVP Arena. The current version of the franchise was established in 2023 and competed in the revived Arena Football League in 2024, where they reached the league championship game. After the AFL ceased operations, the team moved to the new AF1 and quickly became one of its top organizations, building a strong record and winning a league title soon after. The Firebirds continue the long arena-football tradition in Albany and are known for consistent playoff appearances and competitive rosters.

name: Amarillo Warbirds
nameHistory: West Texas Warbirds (2020–2023), West Texas Desert Hawks (2024), Amarillo Warbirds (2026–present)

info: he Amarillo Warbirds franchise traces its roots to West Texas indoor football teams that first began play in 2020 as the West Texas Warbirds in Odessa, Texas. The organization competed in several regional indoor leagues while playing at the Ector County Coliseum and underwent multiple identity and league changes as it searched for long-term stability. Over its existence, the franchise’s league affiliations have included Champions Indoor Football (2020), the Lone Star Series (2021), the Arena Football Association (2022), the Arena Football League (2024), and later the National Arena League (2023, 2026–present). The team briefly rebranded as the West Texas Desert Hawks before eventually relocating to Amarillo, Texas, where it adopted the Amarillo Warbirds name and shifted home games to the Amarillo Civic Center. Despite the relocations, rebrands, and changing leagues, the organization represents a continued effort to sustain professional indoor football in the West Texas region while building a more permanent identity in Amarillo.

name: Anaheim Piranhas
stadiumHistory: MGM Grand Garden Arena (1994), Thomas & Mack Center (1995), Arrowhead Pond of Anaheim (1996–1997)
info: The Vegas Sting were an Arena Football League expansion team that played from 1994 to 1995. Based in Las Vegas, the Sting showed brief competitiveness and reached the playoffs in their inaugural season, but struggled to maintain consistency on the field and at the gate. After two seasons, the franchise relocated to Southern California and became the Anaheim Piranhas in 1996. The Piranhas played two seasons in Anaheim but failed to find success, finishing near the bottom of the standings both years. Continued poor performance and low attendance led to the team folding after the 1997 season, ending a short-lived franchise that never established long-term stability in either market.

name: Arizona Juggernauts
info: One of the IAL's debut teams for 2026. Arizona would have a solid year, going 7-4 before losing to both championship contenders in the double-elimination style playoff bracket.

name: Arizona Rattlers
info: The Arizona Rattlers joined the Arena Football League in 1992 and quickly became one of the league’s most successful and recognizable franchises. Under longtime coach Danny White, the Rattlers became a consistent contender, reaching multiple ArenaBowls and capturing titles in 1994 and 1997. After the AFL restructured, Arizona continued as a powerhouse through the 2010s, led by head coach Kevin Guy, winning three straight ArenaBowls from 2012 to 2014. The team later transitioned to the Indoor Football League, where they continued their winning tradition and secured championships in 2017 and 2024. Across decades and multiple eras, the Rattlers built a legacy defined by consistent playoff success, dominant rosters, and one of the strongest fanbases in indoor football history.

name: Athens Crush
info: Announced May 24th, 2026. The final 4 team names were announced on 6/30/26. Those 4 being, Hedgehawgs, Bullfrogs, Crush, and Panic. The Crush name was later announced on August 26th. 2026.

name: Augusta Stallions
info: The Augusta Stallions were a professional indoor football team based in Augusta, Georgia that played from 2000 to 2002. Competing in af2, the Arena Football League’s developmental league, the Stallions quickly became a competitive team and made the playoffs in two of their three seasons. Despite solid on-field performance and a growing local fanbase, the franchise struggled with long-term financial stability. After the 2002 season, the team folded, ending a short but successful run that left Augusta without arena football.

name: Bay Area Panthers

info: The Bay Area Panthers are an Indoor Football League (IFL) franchise that began play in 2022, originally branding themselves as the Oakland Panthers before shifting to the broader Bay Area Panthers identity prior to their inaugural season to represent the wider Northern California region. The team was created to return professional indoor football to the East Bay after years without a stable franchise and plays its home games in San Jose, California. The Panthers found immediate success on the field, quickly establishing themselves as one of the league’s top expansion teams and capturing the 2023 IFL National Championship in only their second season. Since their championship run, the Panthers have remained regular playoff contenders and are regarded as one of the IFL’s most successful modern expansion franchises, helping reestablish indoor football’s presence in Northern California.

name: Carolina Rhinos
info: The Carolina Rhinos were a professional arena football team based in Greenville, South Carolina, that competed in the af2, the developmental league for the Arena Football League, from 2000 to 2002. They played home games at the Bi-Lo Center and were one of the original teams in the league’s inaugural season. The Rhinos made the playoffs in their first two seasons, including winning one playoff game in 2001, but after a losing record in 2002 the franchise folded.

name: Cedar Rapids Titans
nameHistory: Cedar Rapids Titans (2012–2017, 2024–present), Cedar Rapids River Kings (2018–2020)
stadiumHistory: ImOn Ice Arena (2012–2013), Alliant Energy PowerHouse (2014–2020, 2024–present)
info: The Cedar Rapids Titans are a professional indoor football team based in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, that first joined the Indoor Football League (IFL) as an expansion franchise in 2012 and competed through the 2020 season. The Titans played their first two seasons at the Cedar Rapids Ice Arena before moving to the Alliant Energy PowerHouse in 2014, where the franchise remained its long-term home and appeared in multiple United Conference championship games during its IFL tenure. During the 2018 season the team was sold to new ownership and rebranded as the Cedar Rapids River Kings, a name it used through the end of its original IFL run; the franchise went dormant for the 2021–2023 seasons before returning in 2024, going back to the Titans name and joined the American Indoor Football (AIF).

name: Charleston Swamp Foxes
info: The Charleston Swamp Foxes were an arena football team based in North Charleston, South Carolina, that competed in the af2 league from 2000 to 2003. They played their home games at the North Charleston Coliseum and were one of the original franchises when the league began. The team made the playoffs once during its existence but generally struggled on the field, and the franchise folded after the 2003 season.

name: Charlotte Rage
info: The Charlotte Rage joined the Arena Football League in 1992 as part of the league’s early expansion. They played at the Charlotte Coliseum and showed flashes of competitiveness but never became a top contender. The Rage reached the playoffs in 1993 and 1994 but were eliminated in the first round both times. Struggles on the field and limited fan traction eventually led to the team folding after the 1996 season. The Rage’s five-year stay is remembered as a brief chapter in AFL history during the league’s mid-1990s growth period.

name: Chicago Bruisers
info: The Chicago Bruisers were one of the original Arena Football League franchises, debuting in the league's inaugural 1987 season. After a shaky 2–4 start with no postseason appearance, the Bruisers exploded in 1988 under Perry Moss, going 10–1–1 and reaching ArenaBowl II before falling short of the championship. In 1989, the team regressed, finishing 1–3, and folded shortly after. Though brief in existence, the Bruisers are remembered as a key early AFL franchise, helping shape the league's foundational era and producing one of the AFL’s first powerhouse seasons in 1988.

name: Cincinnati Rockers
info: The Cincinnati Rockers entered the Arena Football League in 1992 as an expansion franchise and quickly generated early excitement with strong attendance and a playoff appearance in their inaugural season. On the field the team finished 7-3 that first year but could not maintain that momentum in year two, dropping to the bottom of the standings with a 2-10 record in 1993. Financial challenges and declining performance made the franchise short-lived, and the Rockers folded after only two seasons. Although brief, their run is remembered for a fast start followed by an equally fast drop that closed the Cincinnati chapter of early AFL history.

name: Cleveland Gladiators
nameHistory: New Jersey Red Dogs (1997–2000), New Jersey Gladiators (2001–2002), Las Vegas Gladiators (2003–2007), Cleveland Gladiators (2008–2017)
locationHistory: East Rutherford, New Jersey (1997–2002), Las Vegas, Nevada (2003–2006), Paradise, Nevada (2007), Cleveland, Ohio (2008–2017)
stadiumHistory: Continental Airlines Arena (1997–2002), Thomas & Mack Center (2003–2006), Orleans Arena (2007), Quicken Loans Arena (2008–2017)
info: The franchise began as the New Jersey Red Dogs in 1997 and quickly became a competitive team in the early years of the AFL’s growth, playing in East Rutherford through the 2000 season. In 2001 the team rebranded as the New Jersey Gladiators, then relocated after the season and became the Las Vegas Gladiators in 2003. The move to Nevada brought a new market but limited on-field success, and after several seasons the franchise relocated again to Ohio, becoming the Cleveland Gladiators in 2008. Cleveland proved to be the team’s most stable era, highlighted by multiple playoff appearances and a run to ArenaBowl XXVII in 2014. The franchise remained active until the AFL shutdown following the 2017 season, ending a twenty-year history that spanned three states and four identities.

name: Cleveland Thunderbolts
stadiumHistory: Ohio Expo Center Coliseum (1991), Richfield Coliseum (1992–1994)
info: The Cleveland Thunderbolts were an Arena Football League team that originally began as the Columbus Thunderbolts in 1991 before relocating to Cleveland in 1992. The move provided a fresh start, and the Bolts made the playoffs in their first Cleveland season despite a losing record, but the success was short-lived. Over the next two years the team struggled both on the field and at the box office, finishing near the bottom of the standings and failing to build long-term stability. After the 1994 season the Thunderbolts folded, ending a brief run marked by flashes of promise but overshadowed by financial and performance challenges common among early AFL franchises.

name: Columbus Destroyers
info: The franchise began as the Buffalo Destroyers in 1999, bringing Arena Football League action to western New York and quickly becoming a competitive team. After the 2003 season, the team relocated to Ohio and became the Columbus Destroyers in 2004. Based in Columbus, the franchise continued to be a regular playoff contender and make the ArenaBowl XXI in 2007, but lost. Following the AFL shutdown after the 2008 season, the team ceased operations, but the Columbus Destroyers name returned briefly in 2019. The franchise is remembered for sustained competitiveness across two cities despite never winning an ArenaBowl title.

name: Connecticut Coyotes
info: The Connecticut Coyotes were an Arena Football League franchise that played from 1995 to 1996. Based in Hartford and playing their home games at the Hartford Civic Center, the Coyotes struggled throughout their existence and rarely found success on the field. Despite frequent coaching changes and attempts to rebuild the roster, the team consistently finished near the bottom of the standings and failed to make a lasting impact in the league. Declining attendance and ongoing financial issues eventually led to the franchise folding after the 1996 season. The Coyotes are remembered as a brief and difficult chapter in AFL history during the league’s rapid expansion era.

name: Dakota Bucks
info: The Bismarck Bucks were a professional indoor football team based in Bismarck, North Dakota, that began play in 2017 as a member of the Champions Indoor Football (CIF) before moving to the Indoor Football League (IFL) in 2019. The franchise was created to bring professional indoor football back to the Bismarck market and played its home games at the Bismarck Event Center. The Bucks were competitive in their early CIF seasons, earning playoff appearances and building a loyal regional fan base, but after facing increased competition and organizational challenges in the IFL, the team ultimately went dormant in 2022. After a rebrand in to 2024 to the Dakota Bucks, they looked to return for 2025, but nothing ever came.

name: Dallas Bulls
info: The Dallas Bulls were removed from the NAL in April 2026, citing contractual obligations were not fufilled. Dallas has cited the have not folded, and will return.

name: Dallas Texans
info: The Dallas Texans joined the Arena Football League in 1990 and quickly made an impact, reaching ArenaBowl IV in their inaugural season behind head coach Ernie Stautner, though they fell short of the title. Despite early success, the Texans could not maintain consistent performance, cycling through coaches including Drew Pearson, John Paul Young, and Jerry Trice over the next three years. They made multiple playoff appearances but never secured a championship, and declining results along with financial issues eventually caught up to the franchise. After the 1993 season, the Texans folded, closing the chapter on a four-year run that featured flashes of promise but never translated into long-term stability.

name: Denver Dynamite
info: The Denver Dynamite was one of the debut Arena Football League teams in 1987. They would go 4-2 and win ArenaBowl I in their debut season, beating the Pittsburgh Gladiators 45-16. Owner Sidney Shlenker would sell the team in 1988 to Gary Graham after sitting the season out. The Dynamite would make it back to play offs in each of their last 3 seasons, but failed to make it back to the ArenaBowl. After the 1991 season, the franchise was sued by their public relations firm and filed for bankruptcy.

info: The Florida Bobcats franchise began in 1992 as the Sacramento Attack before relocating to Florida the following year. They first played in Miami under the name Miami Hooters and later rebranded as the Florida Bobcats, moving to West Palm Beach and later Sunrise. On the field the team struggled for most of its existence, rarely posting winning records and never advancing deep into the playoffs. Despite occasional competitive moments, fan support declined over time and financial stability became an ongoing issue. After years of limited success and little traction in the market, the Bobcats folded following the 2001 season, closing out a ten-year run that moved through multiple cities and identities without finding long-term success.

name: Fort Worth Cavalry
info: The Fort Worth Cavalry were an Arena Football League franchise that played a single season in 1992. Based in Fort Worth, Texas, the team struggled from the start and finished with one of the worst records in the league. Poor on-field performance combined with low attendance and financial issues quickly doomed the franchise. After just one season, the Cavalry folded, making them one of the shortest-lived teams in AFL history and a brief footnote in the league’s early expansion period.

name: Frisco Fighters
info: The Frisco Fighters were an Indoor Football League (IFL) expansion franchise based in Frisco, Texas, that began play in 2021 with the goal of bringing stable professional indoor football to the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex. Playing their home games at the Comerica Center, the Fighters quickly became competitive, posting winning records and earning playoff appearances in their first few seasons while building a strong local fan base in the North Texas sports market. The organization was known for consistent coaching and high-scoring offenses, which helped establish them as one of the league’s more promising modern expansion teams. However, after the 2023 season the franchise went dormant in 2024, pausing operations despite its early on-field success and leaving its long-term future in the league uncertain.

name: Georgia Force

info: The Georgia Force started as the Nashville Kats joining the AFL in 1997. The Nashville Kats would play in Tennessee for five seasons, making the Arena bowl twice but losing in both 2000 and 2001. After the 2001 season the team decided to move to Georgia and rebrand as the Georgia Force. The Georgia Force would play seven seasons through 2008, but would fail to make it back to the Arena Bowl. After the AFL suspended play in 2009, the team would essentially fold. In 2011 the Alabama vipers would move to Georgia and resume the Georgia Force name and legacy. In the two seasons they played they would make a playoffs twice but lose to the Jacksonville sharks both times. After the 2012 season that franchise would fold. In 2024 there was a new Georgia Force franchise under the newly established Arena Football One.

name: Grand Rapids Rampage
info: The Grand Rapids Rampage joined the Arena Football League in 1998 and quickly became one of the league’s strongest expansion teams. Playing their home games at Van Andel Arena, the Rampage were competitive almost immediately and reached ArenaBowl XV in 2001, where they captured the franchise’s only championship. Throughout the early 2000s, Grand Rapids remained a consistent playoff team and developed a strong fanbase in western Michigan. After several seasons of declining performance and the AFL’s broader financial struggles, the Rampage ceased operations following the 2008 season. Their eleven-year run is remembered as one of the more successful mid-market franchises in AFL history, highlighted by sustained competitiveness and a championship title.

name: Green Bay Blizzard
info: The Green Bay Blizzard are a professional indoor football team based in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, part of the Green Bay metropolitan area. Founded in 2003, the Blizzard began play in af2 (the developmental league of the Arena Football League) before joining the Indoor Football League (IFL) in 2010, where they’ve competed ever since. They play their home games at the Resch Center and are known for their high-scoring, fast-paced style of play and strong community engagement. The team has made multiple playoff appearances and won the IFL Eastern Conference title in 2025 under head coach Corey Roberson.

name: Houston ThunderBears
info: The franchise began as the Texas Terror, joining the Arena Football League in 1996 and playing two seasons in Houston. Despite generating early interest, the Terror struggled on the field and failed to become a consistent contender. In 1998 the team rebranded as the Houston ThunderBears in an effort to reset the franchise and build a stronger identity. While the ThunderBears showed occasional improvement, sustained success remained elusive and playoff appearances were limited. Continued performance issues and financial challenges led to the team folding after the 2001 season, ending a six-year run of arena football in Houston under two different names.

name: Indiana Firebirds
info: The Albany Firebirds were one of the most successful franchises of early arena football, joining the AFL in 1990. They quickly became a powerhouse program, making the playoffs in all but one of their Albany seasons and developing one of the sport’s strongest home-field followings. Throughout the 1990s the Firebirds were known for explosive offenses, tough defenses, and multiple deep postseason runs, highlighted by star players and a consistently competitive roster. After ten seasons in New York, the franchise relocated in 2001 to Indianapolis and became the Indiana Firebirds, ending the original Albany era. Though the name would later return under different organizations, the 1990–2000 Firebirds are remembered as a dominant and iconic franchise of the league’s early years.

name: Iowa Barnstormers
info: The Iowa Barnstormers returned to arena football in 2001, bringing the Barnstormers name back to Des Moines for a single season following the franchise’s earlier relocation to New York. After several years away, the team was revived again in 2008 as part of the reorganized indoor football landscape. Since returning, the Barnstormers have remained active through multiple league changes, most notably competing in the Indoor Football League, and have established long-term stability in Des Moines. This modern era has focused on sustained operations and competitive continuity rather than the brief, high-profile AFL success of the 1990s.

name: Jacksonville Sharks
info: The Jacksonville Sharks are a professional indoor football team based in Jacksonville, Florida, that began play in 2010 as a charter franchise of the modern Arena Football League (AFL). Playing their home games at VyStar Veterans Memorial Arena, the Sharks quickly became one of the league’s most successful and best-supported teams, winning the ArenaBowl championship in 2011 and building a strong regional fan base. After the AFL ceased operations, the organization moved to the National Arena League (NAL), where it captured three league championships and remained one of the NAL’s flagship franchises. The team later transitioned to the Indoor Football League (IFL), continuing its long-standing presence in professional indoor football.

name: Jacksonville Tomcats
info: The Jacksonville Tomcats were an arena football team from Jacksonville, Florida, that competed in the AF2 league, the developmental league for the Arena Football League, from 2000 to 2002. They were one of the charter franchises when the league began play. The team played its home games at the Jacksonville Coliseum and finished with winning records in its first two seasons, including a playoff appearance in 2000. Attendance declined over the three seasons and after the 2002 campaign the franchise was folded.

name: Jersey Bearcats
locationHistory: Jackson, New Jersey (2021-2022), Roselle, New Jersey (2023-present)
info: The Jersey Bearcats are a professional indoor football team based in Roselle, New Jersey. Founded in 2018, they began play in 2019 and have competed in leagues such as the Mid-Atlantic Indoor Football League and the American Arena League/American Arena League 2 (AAL/AAL2). The team is owned by AJ Roque and Jermaine Sanders, with Roque also serving as head coach and general manager, and they play their home games at the Warinanco Sports Center. The Bearcats won the AAL2 championship in 2023 and have made multiple playoff appearances. They moved back up to the American Arena League for the 2026 season after several competitive seasons in the AAL2.

info: The franchise began as the Topeka Knights in 1999 and competed through 2000 before rebranding as the Topeka Kings. In 2001 the team became the Tennessee ThunderCats and played two seasons in Tennessee before changing its name to the Tennessee Riverhawks in 2003. After another move and rebrand, the franchise became the Greenville Riverhawks for the 2004 season. The team then relocated to Johnstown, Pennsylvania and became the Johnstown Riverhawks in 2005, where they played through the 2008 season. Throughout its various identities, the franchise experienced frequent relocations, limited on-field success, and ongoing league instability. After the 2008 season the Riverhawks folded, ending a nine-year journey through multiple cities and names.

name: Lincoln Capitols
info: The franchise began as the Lincoln Lightning in 1999, bringing indoor football to Lincoln, Nebraska during a period of rapid growth for lower-level indoor leagues. The Lightning struggled to establish consistent success on the field and faced the same instability that affected many teams at the time. In 2002 the team rebranded as the Lincoln Capitols in an effort to reset the franchise and strengthen its local identity. Despite the name change, results remained limited and long-term stability proved elusive. After the 2006 season, the franchise folded, ending an eight-year run of indoor football in Lincoln marked by persistence but little sustained success.

name: Los Angeles Cobras
info: The Los Angeles Cobras were a short-lived Arena Football League franchise that played only in the 1988 season. Coached by Ray Willsey, the Cobras finished 5-6-1, becoming the first team in AFL history to record a tie. Despite featuring notable talent including quarterback Matt Stevens and receiver Gary Mullen, the team struggled to gain fan traction in Southern California. They reached the playoffs in their lone season but were eliminated in the semifinals, and folded shortly afterward. Though brief in existence, the Cobras remain a unique early footnote in AFL history.

name: Massachusetts Marauders
info: The Detroit Drive were one of the most dominant franchises in early Arena Football League history, debuting in 1988. In just six seasons, they appeared in five straight ArenaBowls, winning four championships (1988, 1989, 1990, 1992) and becoming the league’s first dynasty. After the 1993 season, the franchise relocated to Worcester, Massachusetts, rebranding as the Massachusetts Marauders for 1994. Despite fielding a competitive roster and finishing 8–4, financial struggles and poor attendance led the team to fold after just one season in New England. Though short-lived under the Marauders name, the franchise remains remembered for its Detroit era dominance and early AFL legacy.

info: Part of the 2nd Arena Football League test game, played in 1987. Beat the Chicago Bruisers 33-30. The team was not based in Miami despite the name.

name: Milwaukee Mustangs
info: The Milwaukee Mustangs joined the Arena Football League in 1994 and quickly became one of the league’s stronger teams during the late 1990s. Playing at the Bradley Center, the Mustangs were consistent playoff contenders and captured a Central Division title in 1997. Despite regular postseason appearances and solid fan support, Milwaukee was never able to reach or win an ArenaBowl. After the 2001 season, the Mustangs lost their lease at the Bradley Center and decided to fold. The Mustangs are remembered as a competitive and stable AFL team that enjoyed sustained success but ultimately ended without a championship.

name: Minnesota Fighting Pike
info: The Minnesota Fighting Pike were an Arena Football League expansion team that played only during the 1996 season. Based in Minneapolis and playing their home games at Target Center, the team struggled from the start and finished with one of the worst records in the league. On-field difficulties and lack of traction in the market led to the franchise folding after just one year. The Fighting Pike remain a brief footnote in AFL history, remembered as a short-lived experiment during the league’s mid-1990s expansion period.

name: Minnesota Monsters
info: The franchise now known as the Minnesota Monsters began in 2024 as the Duluth Harbor Monsters, an indoor football team based in Duluth, Minnesota. The organization found quick success on the field, building a strong local fan base and winning back-to-back TAL championships in its first two seasons of play. Following those early titles, the team joined the AF1, and rebranded to the Minnesota Monsters, continuing its history under the new Minnesota name while maintaining continuity with the original Harbor Monsters franchise.

name: Mississippi Wolfpack
info: The Mississippi Wolfpack are a professional arena/indoor football team based in Mississippi that competes in the American Arena League (AAL). Originally successful in the AAL’s developmental tier (AAL2), where they won the 2025 championship, the Wolfpack earned promotion to the AAL for the 2026 season.

name: Nashville Kats (AF1)
info: The Nashville Kats are a professional indoor football team based in Nashville, Tennessee, created as a modern revival of the historic Arena Football League brand that previously operated in the city during the late 1990s and 2000s. The new franchise began play in 2024, bringing arena football back to Nashville after several years without a stable indoor team. Playing their home games at Bridgestone Arena, the Kats were established to capitalize on the city’s strong sports market and nostalgia for the original Kats organization. While still in their early years, the revived franchise focuses on rebuilding the recognizable Kats identity, engaging longtime fans, and reestablishing professional indoor football as a consistent presence in Nashville’s sports landscape.

name: Nebraska Danger
info: The Nebraska Danger were a professional indoor football team based in Grand Island, Nebraska, that began play in 2011 as a member of the Indoor Football League (IFL). The franchise was created to bring professional indoor football to central Nebraska and played its home games at the Heartland Events Center, quickly developing a loyal local fan base. The Danger were competitive throughout much of their existence, earning multiple playoff appearances and regularly finishing near the top of their conference standings. Known for strong community support and consistent attendance, the organization became one of the IFL’s more stable small-market teams during the 2010s. Financial and ownership challenges eventually led to the team ceasing operations after the 2019 season, ending nearly a decade of indoor football in Grand Island.

name: New England Steamrollers
info: The New England Steamrollers joined the Arena Football League as an expansion team in 1988. Based in Providence, Rhode Island and led by head coach Babe Parilli, the Steamrollers finished their lone season 3–9, missing the playoffs. Despite efforts to build a fanbase and early promise from quarterback Brent Pease, the franchise faced financial challenges and low attendance. After just one season, the Steamrollers folded in 1989. Although short-lived, they remain part of the league’s early expansion era, representing the AFL’s attempt to reach new markets in the Northeast.

name: New Mexico Chupacabras
nameHistory: Duke City Gladiators (2015–2025), New Mexico Chupacabras (2026–present)
locationHistory: Albuquerque, New Mexico (2015–2019, 2026–present), Rio Rancho, New Mexico (2021-2024)
stadiumHistory: Tingley Coliseum (2015–2019, 2026–present), Rio Rancho Events Center (2021–2024)
info: The New Mexico Chupacabras are a professional indoor football team based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The organization originally began as the Duke City Gladiators in 2015, competing in several indoor leagues and quickly becoming one of the most recognizable minor-league football brands in the Southwest. The Gladiators built a reputation for competitive teams, earning multiple playoff appearances and 2 CIF championships while playing their home games at Tingley Coliseum. In 2021, the Duke City Gladiators relocated their home games from Albuquerque to nearby Rio Rancho, New Mexico, moving into the Rio Rancho Events Center in an effort to secure a more stable venue and expand their regional reach. That same year, the franchise also joined the Indoor Football League (IFL), marking a significant step up in competition and league visibility while continuing to represent the greater Albuquerque metropolitan area. After going dormant in 2025, the franchise later rebranded as the New Mexico Chupacabras for the 2026 season, and moving back to Albuquerque.

name: New Orleans Night
info: The New Orleans Night were an Arena Football League franchise that played two seasons from 1991 to 1992. Despite early hopes of establishing arena football in Louisiana, the Night struggled on the field, finishing 4–6 in their debut season and falling to a league-worst 0–10 the following year. Attendance and performance issues ultimately led to the team folding after the 1992 season. Their brief run is remembered as one of the shorter-lived teams of the AFL’s early expansion era, marking a quick rise and fall in New Orleans arena football history.

name: New York Dragons
locationHistory: Des Moines, Iowa (1995-2000), Uniondale, New York (2001-2008)
stadiumHistory: Veterans Memorial Auditorium (1995–2000), Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum (2001–2008)
info: The New York Dragons were an Arena Football League franchise that began in 1995 as the Iowa Barnstormers before relocating to Uniondale, New York in 2001 and taking the Dragons name. The team played its home games at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum and became a regular playoff participant. Despite winning division titles and making numerous postseason appearances, the Dragons never captured an ArenaBowl championship. The franchise continued in the AFL through the 2008 season but folded when the league suspended operations, closing out a fourteen-year run that included both its Iowa and New York eras.

name: New York Knights
info: The New York Knights were part of the Arena Football League’s 1988 expansion, playing their only season at Madison Square Garden. The Knights struggled on the field, finishing 2–10 and failing to build momentum in a competitive New York sports market. Despite brief flashes of promise, the team never found stability or strong attendance, leading to their fold after the season. Though their run was short, the Knights remain a memorable one-year chapter in early AFL history, known mostly for their unique placement in one of the nation’s biggest sports cities.

name: Norfolk Nighthawks
info: The Norfolk Nighthawks were an arena football team based in Norfolk, Virginia, that competed in the AF2 league from 2000 through 2003. They played home games at the Norfolk Scope arena. The club qualified for the playoffs in its first season but did not return to the postseason in later years and ceased operations after the 2003 season.

name: North Michigan Muskies

name: Northern Arizona Wranglers
info: The Northern Arizona Wranglers are an indoor football team based in Prescott Valley, Arizona, that began play in 2021 as an expansion franchise in the Indoor Football League (IFL). The team was established to bring professional indoor football back to northern Arizona and quickly found success on the field. Playing their home games at the Findlay Toyota Center,after a rough inagural season, they made a major leap in 2022, compiling one of the league’s best records and winning the IFL National Championship in just their second year of existence. Since their championship season, the Wranglers have struggled to be a regular contender in the IFL, failing to reach playoffs since 2023.

info: The Oklahoma Wranglers were the final incarnation of a franchise that began as the Memphis Pharaohs from 1995 to 1996 before relocating to Portland and becoming the Portland Forest Dragons from 1997 to 1999. After the 1999 season, the team moved again and rebranded as the Oklahoma Wranglers, playing in Oklahoma City from 2000 to 2001. Despite the relocation, success did not follow, as the Wranglers struggled on the field and failed to make the playoffs in either season. Ongoing performance issues and limited fan support led to the franchise folding after the 2001 season, ending a multi-city run that never achieved sustained success in the Arena Football League.

info: The Orlando Predators first took the field in 1991 as an expansion team in the Arena Football League. From early on, they quickly established themselves as a powerhouse, making the playoffs nearly every season and becoming known for strong fan support and a barn-burning home-arena atmosphere. Under long-time head coach Jay Gruden during their golden era, the Predators captured ArenaBowl titles in 1998 and 2000 and competed in several other championship games, cementing their status as one of the AFL’s flagship franchises. Through decades of success and standout players (on both offense and defense), Orlando remained a consistent playoff team up until the league’s decline. Ultimately, after the 2016 season the Predators suspended operations, closing a 25-year run that left a lasting legacy on arena football.

info: The franchise began as the Peoria Pirates in 1999, becoming one of the most successful teams in early af2 history. Playing in Peoria, the Pirates were a consistent contender and won multiple ArenaCup championships, establishing a strong reputation as a model developmental franchise. In 2005 the team rebranded as the Peoria Rough Riders, but the change did not bring the same level of success, and the team struggled to recapture its earlier momentum. After the 2006 season, the franchise left the market before returning briefly as the Peoria Pirates in 2008. The revived Pirates played two more seasons before folding after 2009, closing the book on a franchise remembered primarily for its dominant early run under the Pirates name.

name: Quad City Steamwheelers
info: The Quad City Steamwheelers are a professional indoor football team based in Moline, Illinois, that began play in 2018 as an expansion franchise in Champions Indoor Football (CIF) before joining the Indoor Football League (IFL) in 2019. The team revived the historic “Steamwheelers” name from the Quad Cities’ former arena football club and plays its home games at the Vibrant Arena at The MARK. After competing for one season in the CIF, the franchise moved to the IFL to face higher-level competition and expand its profile. The Steamwheelers’ 2020 campaign was cut short by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the team subsequently went dormant in 2021 due to arena capacity restrictions before returning for the 2022 season. Since their return, Quad City has been a regular Eastern Conference contender, including winning a conference championship in 2022 and making multiple playoff appearances while continuing to build a presence in the IFL’s Midwest footprint

The team experienced its greatest success in 2001, reaching ArenaCup II, but struggled in later seasons. Following financial and ownership issues, the franchise ceased operations after the 2003 season.

name: Salina Liberty
info: The Salina Liberty are a professional indoor football team based in Salina, Kansas, founded in 2015 and beginning play in 2016. The franchise was created to bring professional indoor football back to the Salina market and has played its home games at the Tony’s Pizza Events Center since its inception. The Liberty first competed in Champions Indoor Football (CIF), where they became one of the league’s more consistent teams and eventually won the CIF championship in 2022. Following their success in CIF, the organization later transitioned to the AFL in their 2024 revival, and the follwing AF1 in 2025. The Liberty moved to the NAL for the 2026 season. Throughout their history, the Liberty have maintained stable local support and are known for sustained competitiveness and community involvement in central Kansas indoor football.

name: San Antonio Force
info: The San Antonio Force were a short-lived Arena Football League team that played only during the 1992 season. The Force struggled both competitively and financially, finishing 2-10 and becoming best remembered for a record-setting defensive game in which they lost 50-0, the first shutout in AFL history. Despite attempts to build interest, attendance and performance never reached sustainable levels, and the franchise folded after just one year. Their single-season run stands as one of the briefest in AFL history, a quick experiment that left behind a few memorable moments but no long-term presence in San Antonio.

name: San Antonio Gunslingers
info: The San Antonio Gunslingers are a modern indoor football franchise established in 2022 as a member of the National Arena League (NAL). Based in San Antonio, Texas, the team plays its home games at the Freeman Coliseum and was formed to bring stable professional indoor football back to the city after several earlier franchises had folded or relocated. The Gunslingers were competitive in their early NAL seasons and focused heavily on community engagement and local recruiting. In 2024, the organization moved to the Indoor Football League (IFL), marking a significant step up in league stability and national exposure. Although the team has not yet won a championship, the transition to the IFL positioned the franchise for long-term growth and stronger competition while continuing the long-standing Gunslingers brand in San Antonio indoor football.

name: San Antonio Talons

name: San Diego Strike Force
info: The San Diego Strike Force are a professional indoor football team based in San Diego, California, that began play in 2019 as an expansion franchise in the Indoor Football League (IFL). Formed to reintroduce professional indoor football to the San Diego market, the team plays its home games at Pechanga Arena. After struggling in their inaugural season, the Strike Force gradually improved in subsequent years, building a more competitive roster and increasing community involvement, and they continue working toward regular playoff contention while representing the Southern California indoor football market.

name: San Jose SaberCats
info: The San Jose SaberCats were one of the most successful franchises in Arena Football League history, joining the league in 1995 and playing their home games at the HP Pavilion. After several early playoff appearances, the SaberCats broke through as a dominant force in the 2000s under head coach Darren Arbet. They won ArenaBowl championships in 2002, 2004, 2007 and 2015. They became known for strong defenses and physical play, setting them apart from many offense-driven AFL teams. San Jose consistently contended for division titles and playoff spots throughout their run. Following their championship in the 2015 season, the SaberCats ceased operations, ending a twenty-one year tenure remembered as one of the league’s most stable and championship-caliber eras.

name: Southwest Kansas Storm
info: The Southwest Kansas Storm are a professional indoor football team based in Dodge City, Kansas, founded in 2021 and beginning play in 2022 at United Wireless Arena. The franchise entered competition in Champions Indoor Football (2022–2023) before moving to the Arena Football League in 2024. The organization then made the transition to Arena Football One in 2025, and most recently became a member of the National Arena League beginning in 2026. The team was created as an expansion effort to establish a long-term professional indoor football presence in southwest Kansas, with league transitions reflecting broader changes in the indoor football landscape rather than relocations.

name: St. Louis Stampede
info: The St. Louis Stampede were an Arena Football League expansion team that played in 1995 and 1996 based in St. Louis, Missouri. They played their home games at the Kiel Center and made the playoffs in both seasons but were unable to advance past the first round. Coached initially by Earle Bruce and later by Dave Ewart, the Stampede posted solid records but never found lasting success on the field. After the 1996 season the franchise folded, ending a brief two-year run that remains a part of St. Louis arena football history.

name: Stuttgart Stallions
info: One of the IAL's debut teams for 2026. Stuttgart would play the most games of the debut EU teams, going 1-2, including the only interconference game (excluding the Stars)  before the EU conference would be discontinued midseason.

name: Tampa Bay Storm
locationHistory: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (1987-1990), St. Petersburg, Florida (1991-1996), Tampa, Florida (1997-2017)
info: The longest tenured team in Arena Football League history, the Tampa Bay Storm originally joined the Arena Football League in 1987 as the Pittsburgh Gladiators. The team stayed in PIttsburgh through 1990, playing in ArenaBowl I and III, but would lose both. In 1991, they would move to St. Petersburg, FL, playing in the ThunderDome, and becoming the Storm. The Storm finally got a championship in 1991 after the move, defeating the Detroit Drive 48-42 in ArenaBowl V. Tampa Bay would pick up 3 more championships over the next 5 years (VII, IX, X). In 1997 the Storm would move to Tampa Bay and play in the Amalie Arena, where they stayed until folding in 2017. In 2003, Tampa Bay would get their 5th and last championship in Arena Bowl XVII. During the team's entire 30 year tenure, they played in 10 ArenaBowls, winning 5, and only missed playoffs 6 times.In December 2017, the Storm announced it was ceasing operations due to increasing operating costs combined with decreasing team revenue.

info: The franchise began as the New York CityHawks in 1997, entering the AFL as an expansion team playing at Madison Square Garden. The CityHawks struggled on the field and failed to gain traction in New York, leading to a relocation after the 1998 season. The team moved to Connecticut and became the New England SeaWolves in 1999, showing modest improvement but still limited success in a competitive market. After two seasons in Hartford, the franchise relocated again, this time to Canada, becoming the Toronto Phantoms in 2001. Toronto produced the team’s best run, including a playoff appearance in 2001, but financial and attendance issues persisted. After the 2002 season, the franchise folded, ending a six-year journey across three cities without ever achieving long-term stability.

name: Tucson Sugar Skulls
info: The Tucson Sugar Skulls are a professional indoor football team based in Tucson, Arizona, that began play in 2019 as a member of the Indoor Football League (IFL). Established to bring indoor football back to southern Arizona, the team plays its home games at the Tucson Arena and quickly built a passionate local fan base through strong community outreach and entertaining, high-energy games. In their early seasons the Sugar Skulls became regular playoff contenders and developed a reputation for competitive teams and one of the louder home environments in the league, helping solidify the IFL’s presence in the Southwest.

name: Tulsa Oilers
info: The Tulsa Oilers indoor football team began play in 2023 as an expansion franchise in the Indoor Football League (IFL), using the long-standing “Oilers” sports brand in Tulsa that has been associated with hockey and other professional teams in the city for decades. Based in Tulsa, Oklahoma, the team plays its home games at the BOK Center, one of the largest indoor arenas in the league, and was created to bring modern professional indoor football back to the market after years without a stable franchise. In their inaugural seasons the Oilers focused heavily on community engagement, cross-promotion with the city’s hockey club, and building a competitive roster, quickly establishing a regional fan base. While still a newer organization, the franchise has been viewed as a stable addition to the IFL and an important step in expanding the league’s footprint in the central United States.

name: Vegas Knight Hawks
info: The Vegas Knight Hawks are an Indoor Football League (IFL) expansion franchise that began play in 2022, bringing professional indoor football back to the Las Vegasarea after several earlier arena teams had folded or relocated. Based in Henderson, Nevada, the team plays its home games at Lee's Family Forum. The Knight Hawks were competitive from their inaugural season and quickly built a strong regional fan base thanks to consistent on-field performance and the growing popularity of professional sports in the Las Vegas market. Their breakthrough came in 2025 when the franchise captured its first IFL National Championship, solidifying the team as one of the league’s most successful recent expansion clubs. Since then, the Knight Hawks have been viewed as a stable and rising organization within the IFL, helping strengthen the league’s footprint in the Southwest United States.

name: Washington Commandos
info: The Washington Commandos were one of the original Arena Football League teams, debuting in 1987. They played in the league’s first regular-season game and earned their first win a week later against Denver, finishing the season 2–4. The team sat out 1988 before returning in 1989 under the name Maryland Commandos, but failed to find success and went winless. In 1990 they returned again as the Washington Commandos, playing at the Patriot Center and posting a 2–6 record. Despite never reaching the postseason, the Commandos hold a place in AFL history as one of the league’s foundational franchises, remembered for helping shape the early years of arena football before folding after the 1990 season.

name: Washington Wolfpack
info: The Washington Wolfpack are a professional indoor football team based in Everett, Washington, that began play in 2024 as one of the inaugural teams of the relaunched Arena Football League (AFL). The franchise was announced in 2023 and secured an agreement to play its home games at Angel of the Winds Arena, bringing arena football back to the Puget Sound area after previous Everett teams in indoor leagues earlier in the 2000s. J. R. Wells was named the team’s first head coach, and the Wolfpack debuted in April 2024, drawing attention for historical firsts such as the first female player to score in AFL history while competing against teams like the Oregon Blackbears. After the 2024 AFL season, the Wolfpack joined the newly formed Arena Football One (AF1) in 2025, continuing as members of the West Division and adapting to league changes while building their franchise identity in Everett.

name: Wheeling Miners
info: The Wheeling Miners are a professional indoor football team based in Wheeling, West Virginia. Founded in 2023 and playing their home games at WesBanco Arena, the Miners began play as members of American Arena League 2 (AAL2) in 2024, where they won the championship before briefly joining the National Arena League (NAL) for the 2025 season. In September 2025, the franchise announced its move to the relaunched American Arena League (AAL) for 2026.
